newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Blairs move to new life at No.11.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blairs move to new life at No.11.

text.p: Britain's Prime Minister Tony Blair and his family embarked on a new life on Monday as they moved across London to their official Downing Street home.
The couple's brass bed, wrapped under heavy blankets, was first to leave the Blairs' three-storey north London house, followed by armfuls of suits and shirts, and stacks of crates.
The children joined in to help carry out their belongings, anxiously eyeing them as they piled up in the back of a van.
But in a break with tradition the first family moved into No. 11 and not its better known neighbour No. 10, which had been the prime minister's official residence since 1735.

With three children under the age of 14, the Blair family needed more space than the modest two-bedroom flat at Number 10 could provide, and so swapped with finance minister Gordon Brown, who would traditionally reside at Number 11.
No. 11 has at least four bedrooms and is considerably more spacious than the cramped attic flat next door, which was converted out of servants' quarters 50 years ago.
The two residences share a garden and bachelor Brown presumably does not require as much room for toys, bicycles and roller blades as the five-strong Blair family.

The Blairs considered staying at their 450,000-pound ($725,000) Victorian home in fashionable Islington, but decided it would be unfair to the neighbours because of the security measures that would have had to be taken. Security experts said the family would also be safer at Downing Street.
The Blairs have emphasised that they wish to maintain as normal a life as possible at Downing Street for Euan, 13, Nicholas, 11 and Kathryn, nine.

It is a long time since youngsters lived in Downing Street but Blair -- who turns 44 on Tuesday and is Britain's youngest prime minister since 1812 -- has made great efforts to shield them from the pressures of political life.

His press office sent out a letter on Monday to editors of the British press thanking them for keeping their distance from the young Blairs during the campaign and requesting the children continue to be left alone now their father is in power.

"The family has now moved into No. 11 Downing Street and while obviously the Blairs' domestic arrangements will continue to attract attention, they are hopeful that the children can be left to live as normal a life as possible," the letter read.
One local resident with a particular interest in the new arrangements is Humphrey, a cat adopted by the Cabinet Office at Downing Street in 1989 and listed as the official "mouser".

Cherie Blair is known to dislike cats but has given no indication whether the cat will continue to enjoy free run of the house. Humphrey could be seen wandering cautiously outside the two residences after the family moved in on Monday.
